items: State Legislatures have NO power to establish tribunals under Article 323A; they can only establish tribunals under Article 323B within their legislative field.
Hierarchy of tribunals can be created under Article 323B, but NOT under Article 323A.
Judicial review by High Courts over tribunal decisions remains intact following the landmark L. Chandra Kumar case (1997).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part XIV-A was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
Article 323A deals exclusively with administrative tribunals for public service matters of the Centre, States, local bodies, and public corporations.
Article 323B deals with tribunals for other specified matters such as taxation, foreign exchange, land reforms, and industrial disputes.

Administrative tribunals under Article 323A can be created ONLY by Parliament, whereas tribunals under Article 323B can be created by both Parliament and State Legislatures within their legislative competencies.
There is no hierarchy of tribunals under Article 323A, whereas a hierarchy of tribunals may be established under Article 323B.
